set.hook: A family house on Plaça de Sant Pere, by the fishing port, where the Palamós red prawn is grilled plainly.
set.why: La Gamba has fed Palamós since the 1960s (the old record says 1967, under the Cuadrat family), a few steps from the quay where the town's red prawn is sold at auction each afternoon. Time Out calls it a family restaurant with very little embellishment in the cooking, and that is the point: the gamba goes on the grill with salt. The other house plates are older Empordà ideas, chicken with lobster and black rice.
set.verdict: For anyone who wants the gamba de Palamós a short walk from where it is landed, without a tasting menu around it. Order the grilled prawns first, then a rice; reviews in April 2026 were split, so judge on the prawn.

set.hook: A few tables in a Roses back street where Rafa Cantero cooks the morning's shellfish on a hot plate.
set.why: Rafa Cantero has run this small room on Carrer de Sant Sebastià for more than three decades; Jancis Robinson wrote in 2013 of thirty years at the planxa, with Rosa serving. set.hook: Watch the Palamós catch sold at the falling-price auction, then cook fish with the quay's own kitchen.
set.why: The Palamós fish market sells its catch by Dutch auction: the price falls on a board until a buyer stops it. The Museu de la Pesca runs half-hour guided visits that explain the bidding live through a large window over the floor, usually at 4.30pm and 5pm; they cost EUR 3.50 in 2025. Next door, the Espai del Peix kitchen teaches what to do with the less famous fish, and cooked at the 11th Fira de la Gamba on 13 June 2026.
set.verdict: The best hour in Palamós for a chef or a curious guest: book the auction visit first, then eat the prawn on the port. Check dates before going, since visits run on set days rather than every weekday.

set.hook: L'Escala's oldest salting house: anchovies cured on site since 1888, with a museum and a tasting terrace.
set.why: The Solés family has salted anchovies in L'Escala since 1888, and the factory stands in the oldest salting building left in the town. set.hook: Girona's municipal food hall, opened in November 1944, where the stalls trade from early morning.
set.why: The Mercat del Lleó opened on 3 November 1944, in a building whose architects were chosen by the Franco regime after the Civil War, and it is still the city's main covered food market. Stallholders start early: a 2008 report noted many of them begin winding down well before lunchtime, which is why a Friday-afternoon opening was debated then. Inside are Girona's butchers, fishmongers, cheese and charcuterie counters, and in autumn the wild mushrooms.
set.verdict: Go in the morning, before the counters thin out, and shop for the galley or a picnic: botifarra, Empordà cheese, autumn bolets. Pair it with coffee in the Old Town across the river.

port.title: Prawns, planxa and suquet
port.story: On this coast the fishing ports feed their own back streets, and the cooking stays close to the boat. In Palamós the red prawn is sold by falling-price auction each afternoon, and La Gamba, on Plaça de Sant Pere since the 1960s, grills it with salt a short walk from the quay. Up the coast in Roses, Rafa Cantero has run a few tables on Carrer de Sant Sebastià for more than thirty years, cooking whatever comes in on the planxa with no printed menu. In L'Estartit, opposite the Medes islands, Cal Tet is a family hotel whose ground floor is a marisqueria serving suquet and seafood rice at lunch and dinner.
port.where: La Gamba, Palamós; Rafa's, Roses; Cal Tet, L'Estartit

larder.title: Auction, salt and market
larder.story: The Costa Brava larder runs from the quay to the city. At the Llotja de Palamós the catch is sold by Dutch auction, the price falling until a buyer stops it, and the Museu de la Pesca explains the bidding on half-hour visits over the floor, EUR 3.50 in 2025. In L'Escala the Solés family has salted anchovies since 1888, in the town's oldest salting building, and opened a museum inside the factory for its 130th anniversary. Inland, Girona's covered Mercat del Lleó opened on 3 November 1944 and still trades from early morning, Monday to Saturday, with mushrooms, botifarra and Empordà cheese.
larder.where: Espai del Peix / Llotja de Palamós, Palamós; Anxoves Solés, L'Escala; Mercat del Lleó, Girona

bars.title: Coffee, tapas and the cone
bars.story: Girona's Old Town eats and drinks in small rooms within a few streets of the Onyar. La Fábrica, on Carrer de la Llebre, was opened in March 2015 by the Canadian rider Christian Meier and his wife Amber, and became the morning stop for the professional cyclists who base themselves in the city. Rocambolesc, Jordi Roca's ice-cream shop, began as the dessert trolley at El Celler de Can Roca and opened on Carrer de Santa Clara in 2012; its panet is ice cream in warm brioche. At the top of Carrer de la Força, La Tabarra serves cold, hot and sweet tapas to loud music, though its 2026 trading is unconfirmed.
